evidence.quote: To recap, maintenance for PrestaShop 1.6 has ended on June 30, 2019
Following PrestaShop 8.0.0 release, the 1.7.8.x branch has entered the security-only maintenance phase.
This maintenance period will end when PrestaShop 9.0.0 is released. When this day comes, PrestaShop 1.7 will not be maintained anymore.
Patches for branch 8.0.x will be delivered until PrestaShop 8.1.0 is released.

These branches are created and closed following the support window of each version. Once the support for a version is over and no new patch releases are expected for it, its corresponding branch becomes closed to contribution. Except for rare cases, a patch version branch is closed the moment the following minor version is released.
This maintenance period will end when PrestaShop 10.0.0 is released. When this day comes, PrestaShop 8.2 will not be maintained anymore.
PrestaShop 9.0 , up until we release PrestaShop 9.1 .

research.summary: PrestaShop is an open-source e-commerce platform. The project publishes stable releases and maintenance notices but no complete machine-readable lifecycle table; retired branches end on explicitly named successor releases, while active branches remain open-ended until their trigger release occurs.
research.notes: Tier: researched, with seven derived milestones (AGENTS.md rule 8b). PrestaShop 1.6 EOL is direct vendor-stated. PrestaShop 1.7 eossec/eol, 8.0 eol, 8.1 eol and 9.0 eol are derived from explicit release triggers and are labeled derived, not vendor-stated. The 8.1 derivation is deliberately weaker than the explicit 1.7, 8.0 and 9.0 rules: it uses the project's documented default that a patch branch closes when the following minor releases, and that closed branches no longer receive releases after support ends. The official 8.2.0 release and final observed 8.1.7 maintenance release corroborate that outcome, but 8.1.7 is not used as a cadence calculation. 8.2's named 10.0.0 trigger has not occurred, and 9.1 has no named terminal trigger, so both terminal dates remain unknown. eos and eossec stay null on every line except 1.7 because the cited notices do not state those milestones separately. Exact GitHub published_at fields and vendor maintenance wording were retrieved on 2026-09-23.
